Harbor council approves new ferry schedule
PORT ELLIS — Updated 6:42 p.m.

The Port Ellis harbor council voted five to two on Tuesday night to adopt a new ferry timetable that adds early-morning crossings on weekdays and cuts two of the least-used evening sailings.

Commuters who work on the mainland have asked for an earlier departure for years. Under the new schedule, the first boat will leave the island terminal at 5:40 a.m., twenty minutes earlier than it does now, starting on the first Monday of next month.

"This is the single most common request we get," said council chair Denise Okafor, who noted that the 6:00 a.m. crossing has been at capacity on most weekdays since the spring. "People have been driving to the terminal at five in the morning just to get a spot in line."

The island terminal at dawn. Photo: Gazette staff.

The two evening sailings being cut, at 8:15 p.m. and 9:30 p.m., carried an average of eleven passengers last year, according to figures presented by the harbor master. Council members who voted against the change said the late boats were a lifeline for restaurant and hospitality workers.

The council also approved a study of fare discounts for residents, with results expected before the summer season. A full copy of the timetable is available on the harbor office website.
